_note: Week of June 1–7, 2026. Mediterranean T2D. 190lb 67M lightly active, retired. <80g carbs/day, ~135g protein, ~95g fat, ~1900 kcal. Heart+brain health emphasis: omega-3s, olive oil, avocado, varied nuts. 1 bell pepper total. Max 2 cucumbers. Olives in sauces only. No raw onion. Bedtime snack nightly. Sardine toast has whipped feta spread.

breakfasts.name: Mediterranean Yogurt Bowl with Walnuts & Berries
breakfasts.note: Walnuts are one of the best foods for heart and brain — high in ALA omega-3s and shown to reduce LDL. The berries add antioxidants without much sugar. No grains.
steps: Thaw berries overnight in the fridge.
Spoon yogurt into bowl. Top with berries, walnuts, flaxseed, chia.
Eat slowly — this is a good way to start the week.

breakfasts.name: Two-Egg Scramble with Spinach & Avocado
breakfasts.note: Avocado replaces any toast carbs and adds monounsaturated fat — excellent for heart health and keeps you full well into the afternoon. Zero grain today.
steps: Heat olive oil in a small non-stick pan over medium.
Add spinach and tomatoes, stir 1 min until spinach wilts.
Crack in eggs, scramble gently until just set. Season with oregano, salt, pepper.
Plate eggs with sliced avocado alongside. A squeeze of lemon on the avocado if you have it.

breakfasts.name: Sardine Toast with Whipped Feta & Lemon
breakfasts.note: This one's worth trying even if sardines on toast sounds rough — the whipped feta spread changes everything. Creamy, salty, rich. The sardines just add a savory depth on top. High omega-3, excellent for heart and brain.

ingredients.item: Sardines in olive oil — 1/2 can (~50g), drained
Greek yogurt — 1 tbsp (to whip the feta)

steps: Make whipped feta: mash feta + 1 tbsp Greek yogurt + a squeeze of lemon with a fork until smooth and spreadable. Takes 1 minute.
Toast the bread.
Spread whipped feta generously on the toast.
Lay sardines on top. Crack black pepper, pinch of oregano, squeeze of lemon.
Cherry tomatoes on the side.

breakfasts.name: Pistachio & Walnut Yogurt Bowl
breakfasts.note: Pistachios are lower carb than most nuts and rich in lutein — good for eye and brain health. Combined with walnuts you get a broad range of healthy fats in one bowl.
steps: Thaw berries overnight.
Spoon yogurt into bowl. Top with pistachios, walnuts, flaxseed, chia, berries.

breakfasts.name: Greek Egg & Veggie Bake (makes 2 — save half for lunch)
breakfasts.note: Takes 25 min but earns its keep: you get breakfast now and an easy Friday lunch later. Good project for a slow morning.

ingredients.item: Dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Heat olive oil in a small oven-safe skillet over medium.
Add tomatoes and spinach, cook 3 min. Season with oregano, garlic powder, salt.
Crack in 4 eggs evenly. Scatter feta on top.
Bake 12–14 min until whites set, yolks slightly soft.
Cut in half — eat one half now, cover and refrigerate the other for lunch.

breakfasts.name: Almond & Pecan Overnight Oats
breakfasts.note: Pecans are one of the highest-antioxidant nuts — great for brain health and rarely used, so this adds real variety. Make Friday night, grab Saturday morning.

ingredients.item: Frozen mixed berries — 1/4 cup (add in the morning)

steps: Friday night: combine oats, yogurt, chia, flaxseed, and almond milk in a jar. Stir, seal, refrigerate.
Saturday morning: top with pecans, almonds, and thawed berries.
Eat cold. Add a splash more almond milk if too thick.

breakfasts.name: Full Mediterranean Egg Plate
breakfasts.note: Sunday deserves a proper sit-down. Modeled after a Turkish-style spread — eggs, tomatoes, feta, a few things on the side. Fifteen minutes, no rush.

ingredients.item: Eggs — 2 large, fried in olive oil or soft-boiled

steps: Fry eggs in olive oil over medium-low until whites just set, or soft-boil 7 min.
Arrange everything on a plate: eggs, tomatoes, avocado slices, feta crumbled over.
4 olives on the side — they're mixed in with the tomato and feta so you won't notice them much.
Drizzle a little olive oil over the vegetables. Season with oregano, salt, pepper.
Eat slowly. It's Sunday.

lunches.name: Grilled Chicken & Avocado Bowl
lunches.note: No grains — avocado and olive oil carry the fat calories. Spinach, tomatoes, a few olives folded into the dressing so you barely notice them individually. Clean, filling, very low carb.

ingredients.item: Kalamata olives — 5, roughly chopped (folded into dressing)

steps: Season chicken with garlic powder, oregano, salt. Pan-sear 5–6 min per side or bake 400°F for 22 min.
Finely chop the olives and whisk into olive oil + lemon + oregano dressing — they disappear into the flavour.
Build bowl: spinach base, cherry tomatoes, avocado. Slice chicken on top.
Pour dressing over everything.

lunches.name: Tuna-Stuffed Avocado
lunches.note: No cooking at all. Avocado replaces any grain. High omega-3, very low carb, done in 5 minutes.

ingredients.item: Canned tuna in water — 1 can (142g), drained well

steps: Drain tuna well. Mix with lemon juice, olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and quartered tomatoes.
Halve avocado, remove pit. Scoop a little extra out of each half to make room.
Fill both halves with tuna. Eat straight from the skin.

lunches.name: White Bean & Tomato Skillet (No Fish)
lunches.note: A lighter Wednesday lunch since dinner is more substantial. Cannellini beans with canned tomatoes, olive oil, spinach — ready in 15 minutes. One of those things that tastes way more complex than the ingredient list suggests.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, red pepper flakes, oregano, salt

steps: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium. Add garlic powder + red pepper flakes + oregano, stir 30 sec.
Add tomatoes + beans. Simmer 8 min until slightly thickened. Season with salt.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Finish with lemon.
Eat from the pan — no need to plate fancy.

lunches.name: Lentil & Feta Salad with Brazil Nuts
lunches.note: Brazil nuts appear nowhere else this week — 2 Brazil nuts gives you more than a full day's selenium, which supports thyroid and immune function. Lentils are the lowest-GI legume. Good combo.

ingredients.item: Lentils (dry green) — 45g dry, cooked and cooled

steps: Cook lentils: 45g dry + 225ml water, simmer 20 min, drain. Cool 10 min.
Combine with spinach and tomatoes in a bowl.
Dress with olive oil + lemon + cumin + oregano + salt. Toss.
Top with crumbled feta, walnuts, and 2 Brazil nuts broken in half.

lunches.name: Leftover Greek Egg Bake (from Friday breakfast)
lunches.note: The second half of this morning's egg bake. Eat it warm (3 min in a pan) or cold — both work. Add a little olive oil drizzle and some cherry tomatoes on the side.

ingredients.item: Leftover egg bake — 1/2 portion from Friday breakfast
Cherry tomatoes — a small handful, halved

steps: Warm in a non-stick pan over medium-low for 3 min covered, or eat at room temp.
Plate with cherry tomatoes alongside. Drizzle olive oil over everything.

lunches.name: Smoked Salmon & Avocado Plate
lunches.note: No cooking. Smoked salmon is very high in omega-3s — DHA specifically, which is the fat the brain is literally made of. Avocado gives the healthy fat to round it out. Great Saturday lunch.
steps: Arrange spinach on a plate. Lay smoked salmon over the top.
Add avocado slices and cherry tomatoes.
Scatter capers over the salmon.
Dress with olive oil + lemon. Crack black pepper over everything.

lunches.name: Hummus & Chicken Plate
lunches.note: A proper Sunday spread. Slice leftover chicken from dinner batch cook or grill a fresh piece. The hummus and vegetables make it feel like a full meal.
steps: Grill or pan-sear chicken. Slice.
Spread hummus on the plate, drizzle with olive oil, dust with paprika.
Arrange chicken, tomatoes, and spinach around the plate.
Squeeze lemon over everything.

dinners.name: Baked Salmon with Roasted Zucchini & Walnut Gremolata
dinners.note: Gremolata (lemon zest + parsley + chopped walnuts) takes 2 minutes to make and turns a simple baked salmon into something restaurant-quality. Walnuts add crunch and more omega-3s on top of the salmon's own.

ingredients.item: Lemon juice — 2 tbsp + zest of 1 lemon
Fresh or dried parsley — 1 tbsp (for gremolata)

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss zucchini in 1 tbsp olive oil + salt. Spread on sheet pan.
Season salmon with remaining olive oil + lemon juice + paprika + garlic powder.
Roast salmon and zucchini together 18–20 min.
While roasting: mix chopped walnuts + lemon zest + parsley + a pinch of salt in a small bowl. This is your gremolata.
Plate salmon and zucchini. Spoon walnut gremolata over the salmon.

dinners.name: Chicken Thighs with Roasted Zucchini & Eggplant
dinners.note: No bell pepper tonight — zucchini and eggplant do all the work. Eggplant gets almost meaty when roasted well at high heat. Everything on one pan.

ingredients.item: Dried oregano, thyme, garlic powder, salt

steps: Marinate chicken in 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon + oregano + thyme + garlic powder — 20 min min.
Toss zucchini, eggplant, tomatoes in remaining olive oil + salt. Spread on sheet pan.
Nestle chicken among the vegetables. Bake at 425°F for 25–28 min until chicken hits 165°F.
Spoon the pan juices over everything before serving.

dinners.name: White Bean & Tomato Cod Skillet
dinners.note: The same skillet base as Wednesday lunch but with cod nestled in to poach. One pan, very easy. The olive oil carries the meal calorically so no grain is needed.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, red pepper flakes, oregano, salt

steps: Thaw cod in cold water 20 min, pat dry.
Heat olive oil in wide skillet over medium. Add garlic powder + red pepper flakes + oregano, stir 30 sec.
Add tomatoes + beans + chopped olives (they melt into the sauce). Simmer 5 min.
Nestle cod into sauce. Cover, cook 8–10 min until it flakes easily.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Finish with lemon. Serve from the pan.

dinners.name: Turkey & Lentil Stuffed Zucchini Boats
dinners.note: Bell pepper appears here as a 1/4 of one pepper mixed into the stuffing — just enough for colour and flavour without making it the main event. The zucchini boats replace any bell pepper as the vessel.

ingredients.item: Bell pepper — 1/4 of one, finely diced (the only one this week)
Garlic powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt

steps: Cook lentils: 35g dry + 175ml water, simmer 18–20 min. Drain.
Halve zucchini lengthwise. Scoop out a little flesh from the centre with a spoon to make boats. Brush with olive oil.
Brown turkey in a pan over medium-high. Season well. Mix in lentils + tomatoes + diced bell pepper + spices. Simmer 5 min.
Fill zucchini boats with turkey-lentil mixture. Crumble feta on top.
Bake at 375°F for 25 min until zucchini is tender and feta is golden.

dinners.name: Shrimp with Roasted Eggplant & Chickpeas
dinners.note: End-of-week dinner that feels fresh. Shrimp cooks in 5 min. The eggplant and chickpeas roast while you prep. No bell pepper, no cucumber.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss eggplant + chickpeas + tomatoes in 1.5 tbsp olive oil + garlic powder + paprika + salt.
Roast 20 min, toss once at 10 min.
Toss shrimp with remaining olive oil + cumin + paprika + salt.
Push vegetables to edges. Add shrimp to centre. Roast another 5–6 min until pink and curled.
Squeeze lemon over everything. Serve from the pan.

dinners.name: Sardine Puttanesca over Lentils
dinners.note: The puttanesca sauce — tomatoes, a few chopped olives, capers, herbs — is so flavourful that sardines just taste like a meaty protein in it rather than anything 'fishy'. The olives are chopped fine and cooked in so they're more background flavour than anything you're biting into.

ingredients.item: Sardines in olive oil — 1 can (~100g), drained

substitutions.item: Canned tuna in water — 2 cans, drained well
substitutions.note: Lower omega-3 but works great in this sauce.
substitutions.shopping: Canned tuna in water — 2 cans (sardine swap, Sat)

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, red pepper flakes, oregano, salt

steps: Cook lentils: 50g dry + 250ml water, simmer 20 min. Drain, season lightly.
Heat olive oil in pan over medium. Add garlic powder + red pepper flakes + oregano, 30 sec.
Add tomatoes + finely chopped olives + capers. Simmer 10 min until thick.
Break sardines into chunks, nestle into sauce. Heat 2 min.
Stir in spinach until wilted. Squeeze lemon.
Spoon over lentils.

dinners.name: Greek Baked Chicken with Roasted Tomatoes & Hummus
dinners.note: Sunday dinner that sets up next week. Roasted cherry tomatoes instead of any bell pepper — they get jammy and sweet and are arguably better. Hummus on the side for dipping.

ingredients.item: Cherry tomatoes — 200g (large portion — these are the vegetable)
Dried oregano, garlic powder, paprika, salt

steps: Marinate chicken in 1 tbsp olive oil + lemon + oregano + garlic powder + paprika — 30 min.
Toss cherry tomatoes + zucchini in remaining olive oil + salt. Spread on sheet pan with chicken.
Bake at 425°F for 25 min until chicken is 165°F and tomatoes are jammy and blistered.
BATCH COOK WHILE THIS BAKES: Start lentil soup on stove. Hard-boil 4 eggs for bedtime snacks.
Serve chicken + vegetables with hummus on the side. Spoon the tomato juices from the pan over everything.

daytimeSnacks.name: Walnuts & Hard Boiled Egg
daytimeSnacks.desc: 20g walnuts (~10 halves) + 1 hard-boiled egg. High fat, moderate protein, nearly zero carb. Good heart-and-brain combo for a Monday.

daytimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt with Chia Seeds
daytimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 1 tbsp chia seeds. Stir and let sit 5 min to gel. High protein, very low sugar impact.

daytimeSnacks.name: Almonds & a Few Cherry Tomatoes
daytimeSnacks.desc: 28g almonds (~23 almonds) + a small handful of cherry tomatoes. Simple, filling, no blood sugar impact worth worrying about.

daytimeSnacks.name: Smoked Salmon on Cucumber Rounds
daytimeSnacks.desc: 50g smoked salmon on 8–10 cucumber rounds. Top with a tiny squeeze of lemon and crack of pepper. Elegant and zero cooking.

daytimeSnacks.name: Pecans & Walnuts
daytimeSnacks.desc: 15g pecans + 14g walnuts. A simple mixed nut snack with two of the best brain-health nuts available. Good Friday afternoon fuel.

daytimeSnacks.name: Feta & Cherry Tomatoes
daytimeSnacks.desc: 30g feta + a handful of cherry tomatoes. Drizzle of olive oil, pinch of oregano. Zero cooking, very Mediterranean, easy Saturday snack.

daytimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter & Celery
daytimeSnacks.desc: 2 tbsp almond butter with celery sticks for dipping. Good Sunday afternoon while batch cooking is underway.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter on Whole Grain Toast
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: The fat in almond butter slows digestion of the toast carbs, releasing glucose gradually over 4–6 hours — giving your liver something to work with overnight without a spike going to bed.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 slice whole grain toast + 2 tbsp almond butter. No honey. Eat slowly.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt & Walnuts
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Protein digests slowly overnight. The walnuts add fat to slow things further. Research in T2D patients links a Greek yogurt bedtime snack to improved fasting glucose the next morning.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 20g walnuts. Stir together or eat the walnuts on the side.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Hard Boiled Egg & Almonds
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Almost pure fat and protein — virtually no glucose impact. Good after a higher-carb dinner. The small carb from almonds is just enough to prevent overnight lows without any spike.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 hard-boiled egg (from the Sunday batch) + 28g almonds. Salt the egg.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Small Bowl of Lentil Soup
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Lentils have a glycemic index around 32 — one of the lowest of any carb. They digest so slowly they act as a timed-release glucose drip overnight. Good pick after a lighter dinner.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: About 3/4 cup of the batch-cooked lentil soup, reheated. Drizzle of olive oil.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Almond Butter & Celery
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: High fat, moderate protein, very low carb. Good end-of-week option — satisfying without being heavy. The almond butter fat keeps things stable through the night.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 2 tbsp almond butter with 3–4 celery sticks.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Greek Yogurt with Chia & Walnuts
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Protein + fat + chia fiber — everything slows digestion and keeps blood sugar from dropping overnight. This combination is particularly good for sleep quality.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 container plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 1 tbsp chia seeds + 14g walnuts.

bedtimeSnacks.name: Whole Grain Toast with Almond Butter & Flaxseed
bedtimeSnacks.whyItWorks: Same principle as Monday — fat slows carb absorption for a long overnight release. The flaxseed adds extra fiber and omega-3s. A good bookend to the week.
bedtimeSnacks.desc: 1 slice whole grain toast + 2 tbsp almond butter + 1 tbsp ground flaxseed sprinkled on top.

Produce: Cherry tomatoes — 3 pints (~900g, used every day)
Zucchini — 4 medium (Mon dinner + Tue dinner + Thu stuffing boats + Sun dinner)
Avocado — 4 medium (Tue breakfast + Mon lunch + Tue lunch + Sat lunch + Sun breakfast)
Bell pepper — 1 (only 1/4 used in Thu dinner stuffing — rest is yours)
Meat, Fish & Seafood: Sardines in olive oil — 3–4 cans (Wed breakfast + Sat dinner + backup)
Chicken breast — ~700g total (Mon lunch + Sun lunch + Sun dinner + batch)
Canned tuna in water — 1 can (Tue lunch)
Dairy & Eggs: Plain nonfat Greek yogurt — 8 containers (Mon + Thu + Sat breakfast, Wed breakfast spread, Tue + Sat + Sun bedtime snack, Tue snack)
Eggs — 1 dozen (Tue breakfast + Fri breakfast bake + bedtime batch)
Canned & Jarred: Cannellini beans — 2 cans (Wed lunch + Wed dinner)
Lentils, dry green — 400g bag (Thu lunch + Thu dinner + Sat dinner + batch soup)
Diced tomatoes — 4 cans (Wed lunch + Wed dinner + Thu dinner + Sat dinner)
Capers — 1 small jar (Sat lunch + Sat dinner)
Kalamata olives — 1 jar (Mon + Wed + Sat dinner, Sun breakfast — always chopped into sauce)
Hummus — 1 container (~250g, Sun lunch + Sun dinner)
Sardines in olive oil — see Meat & Fish above
Bread, Grains & Nuts: Whole grain bread — 1 loaf (Wed breakfast + Mon/Sun bedtime snack)
Rolled oats (not instant) — small bag (Sat breakfast, ~35g)
Almonds — 1 bag (~150g, Wed snack + Wed/Fri bedtime snack)
Pecans — small bag (~60g, Sat breakfast + Fri snack)
Brazil nuts — small bag (only need 2 for Thu lunch — great selenium source)
Almond butter — 1 jar (Mon/Fri/Sun bedtime + Sun snack)
Unsweetened almond milk — small carton (Sat breakfast)
Pantry & Condiments: Frozen mixed berries — 1 bag (Mon + Thu + Sat breakfast)
Dried oregano — used almost every meal
Garlic powder — used almost every meal
Paprika, cumin, thyme, red pepper flakes
